name: Kilimanjaro by the Machame route
why: The 'whiskey route' up the highest mountain of Africa: rainforest, the moorland of the Shira plateau, the Barranco Wall and the glaciers of the crater rim, down by the Mweka route.
book: Kilimanjaro National Park fees per day, paid through a licensed operator: climbing without a registered guide and porters is not allowed. Most climbs start from Moshi. Seven days gives the best chance of reaching the top.
water: Porters boil stream water at every camp.
dangers: Altitude: the summit is at 5,895 m. Headache, vomiting, confusion or breathlessness at rest: go down at once.
Summit night starts around midnight, -10 to -20 C with wind at the crater rim.
Afternoon storms and hail in the rainy months (March to May, November).
The Barranco Wall is a scramble on rock with hands: easy, but some exposure.
turnaround: Guides turn you back at any sign of altitude sickness. Be at Stella Point by 07:00, or turn back.

points.name: Machame Gate
points.note: The park gate at 1,800 m in rainforest above the village of Machame.

points.name: Shira Cave Camp
points.note: Moorland of giant heather at 3,750 m on the edge of the Shira plateau.

points.name: Barranco Camp
points.note: A camp in a valley of giant groundsels under the Barranco Wall and the Southern Icefield.

points.name: Barafu Camp
points.note: The high camp at 4,670 m on a bare ridge, start of summit night.

points.name: Uhuru Peak
points.note: The 5,895 m summit on the crater rim, with glaciers walls around it.

points.name: Mweka Gate
points.note: The way out through the rainforest, where you get your summit certificate.
